text:
marina: quick update from the long-context quant bakeoff i ran this morning — SQ vs activation-aware AWQ on the new 7B-48k candidate checkpoint. ran fp16 baseline, SQ+INT8, AWQ-FP8, and GPTQ-INT4 variants across the 48k eval set.

alex: great — top-level numbers?

marina: short summary:
- fp16 baseline: MMLU 74.9, perplexity (long-pass) 12.4, mem_kv ~28GB, p95 latency (token) ~9.8ms on v100-dedicated with KV on GPU.
- SQ + INT8: MMLU 74.3 (-0.6), ppl 12.9 (+4%), mem_kv ~20GB, p95 9.6ms. minimal output drift, highest cost win.
- AWQ + FP8 (act-aware scaling): MMLU 73.7 (-1.2), ppl 13.5 (+9%), mem_kv ~18GB, p95 9.9ms. some early-token instability on >32k contexts.
- GPTQ-INT4: MMLU 71.1 (-3.8), ppl 16.8 (+36%), mem_kv ~14GB, p95 10.8ms. clear regression on factual QA.

jin: interesting that SQ preserved accuracy best. did you do activation scaling ablation for AWQ?

marina: yes — ran act_scale in {0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2}. best tradeoff at 0.8: reduced early-token runaway in a few prompts, MMLU moved from 73.7 -> 74.0 but ppl still higher than fp16. act_scale=1.2 reduced ppl but introduced clipping -> hallucinations in long chains.

sam: can you paste the exact command you used? want to reproduce on dedicated pool.

marina: pasted below (used our eval harness):
```bash
python -m infra.eval_bench \
  --model redwood/x7b-48k-candidate \
  --quant_config smoothquant,int8;awq,fp8 \
  --ctx 48000 \
  --batch 1 \
  --eval_set longpass-48k-v1 \
  --output gs://redwood-ml/quant-bakeoffs/1848769999/ \
  --seed 42
```

infra-bot: job launched on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (job id rb-184876-01)

eval-bot: run finished. artifacts: gs://redwood-ml/quant-bakeoffs/1848769999/artifacts.zip. summary.csv attached.

alex: any qualitative failures? examples would help.

marina: flagged two categories: (1) AWQ-FP8 with act_scale=1.0 shows prompt-reset drift after ~36k tokens for chained QA (answers start repeating/contradicting). (2) GPTQ-INT4 loses factual dates / numbers in multi-step math. SQ-INT8 only shows slight tokenization-level differences.

jin: did you try hybrid: SQ for most layers + AWQ on attention-only layers?

marina: yes — hybrid config (SQ all linear layers + AWQ attention) gave MMLU 74.1, ppl 13.0, mem_kv ~19GB. better than AWQ-only, still slightly worse than pure SQ. promising middle ground for constrained memory targets.

sam: what's the recommendation for Dedicated deploys?

marina: for 48k target, recommendation:
- default: SQ + INT8 for prod (best accuracy vs mem tradeoff).
- optional: hybrid SQ+AWQ for customers who need extra memory headroom but can tolerate ~0.4-0.8% accuracy loss.
- avoid GPTQ-INT4 on long-context QA workloads until more reg mitigations are in place.

alex: please create a short RFC for the rollout decision. include cost delta estimates and an A/B rollout plan (canary on 5% traffic).

marina: will do, uploading RFC draft to the eng-ml drive and linking in #eng-ml later. artifacts already uploaded: gs://redwood-ml/quant-bakeoffs/1848769999/.

sam: thanks — can you also attach a couple of failing examples to the RFC? that'll help model owners triage.

marina: yup, added 12 failing transcripts (AWQ-longctx) to the artifacts.zip.

jin: nice work. one follow-up: let's add an eval that measures "answer drift" specifically for sequences >40k. we should automate that as part of model onboarding.

marina: agreed — adding to the onboarding checklist and the eval harness.

alex: +1. thanks for running this so quickly. :thumbsup:
